title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. G is a twisted form of GL(2) over a base S, probably the unit group of a rank-4 Azumaya algebra M; the crossed-out line on the next page reads 'Si M = End(F)'. ρ and σ are sections of G. The page continues the computation on p.478, where ρ was put in normal form (0 u; v w) and σ in normal form (0 u'; v' w'). There the requirement that ε0 and ε1 be standard transverse unipotents forced u' = -u, v' = -v and w + w' = u, i.e. ρ + σ = uP with P = diag(0,1).

Aim. Grothendieck wants intrinsic 'numerical criteria' (traces and determinants) on the pair (ρ, σ) that guarantee this normal form.

Definitions. Put ε0 = -σ^{-1}ρ and ε1 = -ρσ^{-1}. Then ε1 = σ ε0 σ^{-1} = ρ ε0 ρ^{-1}: the two elements are conjugate both by σ and by ρ. The notation σ(ε0) means this inner action.

Proposition: the following are equivalent.
(a) ε0 = 1 + N0 is a regular unipotent: N0 is nilpotent and nonzero at every point (equivalently for ε1 = 1 + N1). Moreover N0 and N1 are nowhere homothetic, i.e. fibrewise independent; equivalently their kernel lines differ at each point.
(b) (32): det σ = det ρ, Tr σ^{-1}ρ = -2, and u := Tr(σ+ρ) is invertible. The first two say det ε0 = 1 and Tr ε0 = 2, i.e. ε0 is unipotent. The third encodes regularity plus independence, by reference to the proposition on p.449'.
(c) (33): det σ = det ρ, det(σ+ρ) = 0, and Tr(σ+ρ) is invertible.
(d) det σ = det ρ, and σ + ρ = uP with P an elementary (rank-1) projector and u in Γ(G_m). Here u and P are unique: u = Tr(σ+ρ) and P = (σ+ρ)/u.
The next page adds two more conditions. (e) There is a unique isomorphism φ: GL(2) → G sending ε1 to (1 0; 1 1) and ε0 to (1 u/v; 0 1). (f) The normal form of p.478.

Proof sketch, partly from the next page; I checked it.
- (b)⇔(c): det(σ+ρ) = det σ · det(1 + σ^{-1}ρ) = det σ (2 + Tr σ^{-1}ρ) once det σ = det ρ.
- Structure of σ+ρ: σ+ρ = -σN0 = -N1σ. So it has rank at most 1, with kernel Ker N0 and image Im N1 = Ker N1.
- (a)⇒(c): its trace is invertible exactly when Im N1 is not contained in Ker N0, i.e. when the kernels of N0 and N1 are distinct. This is the independence condition, and it also forces N0 to be nonzero, i.e. regularity.
- (c)⇔(d): Cayley–Hamilton gives A² = Tr(A)·A for A = σ+ρ, so P = A/u is idempotent of trace 1.

Context. Within 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' this is a normalization lemma: it characterizes those pairs (ρ, σ) in a GL2-form whose associated 'monodromy' elements ε0, ε1 form a standard transverse pair of unipotents. That pair is the image of the standard generators (1 *; 0 1), (1 0; 1 1).
errors: No mathematical error on this page; the equivalences are correct over any base where the 2x2 identities hold.
Condition (b)c) is not derived on this page; it is deferred to 'prop. p.449''. The same fact follows directly from σ+ρ = -σN0 = -N1σ, which the page does not state.
Next page, (f): 'uv' = vw' = 0' cannot be right as transcribed. Consistency with p.478 requires u' = -u and v' = -v (with w + w' = u). Also in (35) the entry '2[?]' should be u/v, as in (38).

ideas.what: Characterizing a pair (ρ,σ) in a form of GL2 by det σ = det ρ, Tr σ^{-1}ρ = -2 and Tr(σ+ρ) invertible, so that -σ^{-1}ρ and -ρσ^{-1} are transverse regular unipotents
ideas.modern_name: trace/determinant (character-variety) coordinates for pairs in GL2 / SL2; normal form of a pair of transverse unipotents
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Fricke–Klein trace coordinates; standard linear algebra)

ideas.what: σ+ρ = uP with P a rank-one idempotent, uniquely determined; obtained via Cayley–Hamilton A^2 = Tr(A)A for a rank-≤1 matrix
ideas.modern_name: rank-one idempotent / elementary projector in an Azumaya algebra of rank 4

ideas.what: Working intrinsically in a twisted form G of GL(2) over a base rather than in matrices, with a unique rigidifying isomorphism GL(2) ≅ G determined by the pair
ideas.modern_name: rigidification of forms of GL2 by a pair of transverse unipotents (trivialization of an Azumaya algebra)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct but elementary linear-algebra normalization lemma that serves the larger 'équation des lacets' computations. Nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'σ(ε0) = ρ(ε0)' denotes the inner action (conjugation) of σ and ρ on ε0.
In (a), the inserted text reads roughly: '1°) ε0 est unipotent régulier (⇔ ε1 ...), 2°) ε0 et ε1 en chaque point indépendants, i.e. posant ...'.
In the margin note, '(-ε0)' in 'det(-ε0)=1' is crossed out, leaving det(ε0) = 1.
